findings.summary: Two of the entries added to HTTP_GROUPS this round -- `org\.springframework\.web` and `com\.sun\.net\.httpserver` -- are not Maven groups and can never match a dependency report line. Spring's group is `org.springframework` (artifact `spring-web`/`spring-webmvc`) or `org.springframework.boot`; `com.sun.net.httpserver` is a JDK package with no coordinate at all. They are inert entries that read as coverage.
findings.failure_scenario: Ran the script's own grep over a synthetic report containing `org.springframework:spring-web:6.1.14`, `org.springframework:spring-webmvc:6.1.14` and `org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web:3.3.4`: zero matches. `io.undertow:undertow-core`, `org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core`, `io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded` and `io.helidon.webserver` all matched, so the seven frameworks from M7 are genuinely covered -- only these two extras are dead. Concretely: `ingest/build.gradle.kts` adding `implementation("org.springframework:spring-webmvc:6.1.14")` resolves clean and prints `ok 1 module(s) checked`. Fix is one character each: `org\.springframework` (the `.boot`/`:spring-web` suffixes are then caught by the following `[.:]`), and drop `com.sun.net.httpserver`, which belongs in the java.net.http prose note directly above rather than in a coordinate denylist that cannot see it.

findings.summary: The comment justifying the compileClasspath pass says "Rule 4 (nothing depends on `http`) is also a compile-time fact", but no check for rule 4 exists anywhere in the script. The comment implies an assertion the gate does not make. Raised late -- it predates this round and I missed it in rounds one and two.
findings.failure_scenario: `plugin/build.gradle.kts` changes `api(project(":client"))` to `api(project(":http"))`. `plugin` is not in NO_HTTP (deliberately -- the consumer needs an HTTP client), so HTTP_GROUPS is never applied to it; NO_CLOUD only greps cloud SDKs; the binstore-backends grep is hardcoded to that one project name. The gate prints ok while Helidon webserver has been pulled transitively into the OpenSearch JVM -- the exact outcome ADR-0019 and rule 2 exist to prevent. The plugin/binstore-backends check added this round is the template: `printf '%s\n' "$deps" | grep -qE "project '?:http'?"` for every module except `http` itself. Either add it or delete the rule-4 clause from the comment; a gate that names a rule it does not check is how the next reader concludes it is covered.
